candidates.draft_body:
Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

Martyrdom climax: a voice from heaven names the three sons EXPLICITLY — Abya, Sila, Fentos (አብያ፥ ሲላ፥ ፈንቶስ) — and commands them to accept martyrdom. They are scourged, imprisoned three days, brought to the public square, tortured. The 'FIVE SONS OF MAQABIS' formulation (developed across chs. 3-4) is DISTINCTIVE to the Ethiopian narrative — it has NO parallel in the LXX 2 Maccabees account of the seven brothers. The bowing-beasts topos is paralleled in Daniel 6:22 and recurs across Christian martyr-acts (e.g. Acts of Paul and Thecla). Three-day imprisonment echoes Jonah 1:17 + Christ's three days in the tomb (Mt 12:40), patristically read as resurrection-figure.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

'But the beasts came roaring and were unleashed upon them; and when they reached the martyrs, THEY BOWED DOWN TO THEM AND PAID THEM HOMAGE' — the BEASTS-BOW-DOWN topos, with the strongest precedent in DANIEL 6:22 (the lions and Daniel) and recurring through Christian martyr-acts (Acts of Paul and Thecla — Thecla preserved by a lioness; Acts of Thomas; Martyrdom of Polycarp). Meqabyan's specific count of SEVENTY-FIVE soldiers killed by the released beasts (3:26) is characteristic of the book's love of numbered enumerations and has no obvious source. The verse establishes the divine-intervention pattern: beasts function as instruments of judgment-reversal, refusing the king's command and executing the king's soldiers instead.

Meqabyan (Ethiopian tradition) First Book of Meqabyan (Mäṣḥafä Mäqabyan I) (c. 600 AD)

Two younger-brothers appear (3:28-30): 'Come, let us flee, lest these criminals and waverers find us.' The martyrs refuse to flee; the two younger brothers join them — making FIVE BROTHERS IN TOTAL. **The 'five sons of Maqabis' formulation is DISTINCTIVE to the Ethiopian narrative** and has NO parallel in the LXX 2 Maccabees account of the seven brothers. The expansion from three-named (Abya/Sila/Fentos) to five-total restructures the Maccabean-martyr-family typology around the Meqabyan-specific five-fold number. Per scholarly apparatus §6 ('The Maqabean Family of 1 Meqabyan'): the five-brothers-of-Maqabis-of-Benjamin in 1 Mq is structurally MIRRORED by the five-sons-of-Maqabis-of-Moab in 2 Mq 13:1 (a NUMBER-SYMMETRY across the two books that supports Horovitz's structural distinction between 1 Mq and 2 Mq).

'And angels received them — the very men who had cast them in seeing it. THEIR SOULS THEY TOOK TO WHERE ABRAHAM AND ISAAC AND JACOB ARE — TO PARADISE WHERE JOY IS FOUND' — angels-receive-souls-to-Paradise martyrdom-completion. The Abraham-Isaac-Jacob destination is the bosom-of-Abraham paradise-locus (Luke 16:22 'carried by the angels into Abraham's bosom'); the triple-patriarch is the standard EOTC formula for the righteous-dead's abode (cf. seed 2:22 invocation). The verse closes the 1 Mq Ch 3 martyrdom-cycle with the canonical angelic-psychopomp motif (parallels Apocalypse of Paul §§14-18 soul-at-death narrative; Testament of Asher 1:3-9). The destination's name-form ('where joy is found,' ደስታ ስፍራ) is a distinctive Tewahedo Paradise-vocabulary.
